title: AWS access key ID
message: AWS access key ID found in source. Treat as compromised: rotate it, then remove it from history.
remediation: Rotate the credential immediately, move it to a secret manager / env var injected at runtime, and purge it from git history.

title: Stripe live key
message: Stripe live key found in source. Treat as compromised: rotate it, then remove it from history.
remediation: Rotate the credential immediately, move it to a secret manager / env var injected at runtime, and purge it from git history.

title: Missing security headers: content-security-policy, strict-transport-security, x-frame-options, x-content-type-options, referrer-policy, permissions-policy
message: Response is missing: content-security-policy, strict-transport-security, x-frame-options, x-content-type-options, referrer-policy, permissions-policy.
remediation: Set these headers at the edge (CDN/reverse proxy) or in the app framework.

title: Server banner discloses version: BaseHTTP/0.6 Python/3.14.7
message: A versioned Server header makes it trivial to match the stack against known CVEs.
remediation: Strip or generalize the Server header at the reverse proxy.

title: Cookie 'sid' missing secure, httponly
message: Cookie is missing: secure, httponly. Without Secure it can be sent over plain HTTP; without HttpOnly, JavaScript (and so XSS) can read it.
remediation: Set Secure; HttpOnly on every cookie that isn't deliberately meant for JS.

title: Cookie 'sid' has no SameSite attribute
message: No SameSite attribute set. Browsers default this to Lax, but an explicit value documents intent and protects older/embedded clients.
remediation: Set SameSite=Lax (or Strict for sensitive session cookies).

title: CORS reflects an arbitrary Origin
message: Access-Control-Allow-Origin echoed back our made-up probe origin ('https://janus-cors-probe.invalid') together with Allow-Credentials: true, meaning any website can read authenticated responses from this origin via a victim's browser.
remediation: Validate Origin against an explicit allowlist server-side; never reflect it verbatim.

title: Potentially exposed path: /.git/config
message: GET /.git/config returned 200 with a body that differs from the baseline 404/fallback, so this looks like a real, reachable endpoint.
remediation: Confirm intent; if unintentional, remove public access or put it behind auth.

title: Auth-protected path confirmed reachable: /admin
message: GET /admin returned 401: the path exists and is protected by authentication. This is expected for admin surfaces; it is reported so the inventory is complete, not as a break-in.
remediation: Confirm the auth layer is intentional and that no weaker path bypasses it.

title: AWS access key ID found in shipped JS bundle
message: AWS access key ID is embedded in a publicly served JS bundle: shipped to every visitor's browser and trivially extractable. Treat as compromised.
remediation: Rotate the credential immediately. Anything that must reach the browser needs its OWN scope restriction at the provider.

title: Publishable key shipped in JS bundle: Stripe live key
message: Stripe live key with a publishable-key prefix is present in client JS. That is expected for this key type, but it must be restricted at the provider (allowed referrers, allowed APIs) or it can be abused for quota/billing.
remediation: Confirm HTTP-referrer and API restrictions on this publishable key.
